value: Prior results remain reproducible where artifacts are available.
A world with at least 10,000 distinct participants.
Participants autonomously browse and consume resources without CAM initiating each event.
Participants return to useful resources and leave unsatisfactory ones.
Independent activity persists over at least 30 simulated days.
Controlled changes to available resources produce measurable differences in behavior.
Actual text, image, audio and video artifacts can be published.
Participants discover content through multiple channels.
Sharing, following and subscriptions affect future interactions.
At least one end-to-end browser-based workflow operates against real simulated state.
At least four genuinely distinct recommendation mechanisms operate end-to-end.
Controlled recommendation changes produce measurably different exposure and consumption patterns.
At least one platform changes distribution behavior during a persistent run.
Participants and creators cannot access hidden evaluator-only algorithm parameters.
Exposure and attention accounting remain consistent.
Actual trained or pretrained encoders process text, image, audio and video artifacts.
Encoders produce materially different representations for appropriate semantic changes.
Controlled artifact changes affect participant behavior through learned representations.
Embedding caches invalidate correctly when content changes.
No reliance on creator-assigned quality scores.
At least three behavioral domains fitted against legitimate empirical data.
Content consumption and randomized commercial-response modeling are mandatory.
At least 256 simultaneously active small adaptive participants in the standard test profile.
Demonstrated neural parameter changes resulting from experience.
Behavioral improvement on a controlled new-condition test.
Measured comparison between compact numerical policies and language-capable alternatives.
At least eight independently operating semantic participants in a standard world.
Real execution of consequential world actions.
At least one independently verified collaborative or productive result.
A scalable population profile supporting at least 10 million distinct simulated identities or explicitly separate estimated-population mode.
Organic propagation through ordinary distribution and consumption mechanisms.
An executable positive-control experiment producing a large adoption cascade.
A scale test demonstrating the ability to process ten million qualifying distinct consumption events.
An agent creates a new executable product or service.
Independent participants test or use it.
Its deployment changes actual world resource consumption.
Detection of circular or related-party transactions.
Agent-created capabilities alter existing world conditions.
New services can address these needs.
At least three independently generated multi-stage causal chains are demonstrated.
Counterfactual removal experiments verify the dependency.
At least 60 admitted structural training families.
At least 20 independent validation or evaluation families.
All ten Tier 1 capability categories represented.
At least one successful feasible reference trajectory per domain.
All major subsystems coexist inside one generated civilization.
At least six types of demonstrated cross-domain effects.
At least three structurally different civilization profiles.
Successful 30-, 90-, 180- and 365-day simulation runs at documented population profiles.
Multiple actual learned policies participate in a shared civilization.
At least two independently updated competing policy groups.
A lightweight reference learner (not CAM) consumes experience and performs parameter updates through the observation-only interface.
An architecture-independent reference learner executes real actions in Tier 1.
An architecture-independent reference learner executes real actions in Tier 2.
An architecture-independent reference learner executes real actions in Tier 3.
Actual experience storage and parameter updates of a lightweight reference learner.
Observation and action schemas shared across Tier 1, 2 and 3 through one learner interface.
Checkpoint persistence of the reference learner.
Curriculum selection based on measured learner behavior.
Evidence that generated worlds target distinct weaknesses.
Development, standard and large population profiles benchmarked.
Peak CPU, RAM and VRAM measured.
No unresolved critical or high-severity security or integrity defects.
No fake, skipped or placeholder acceptance tests.
Use real model execution, not stub vectors.
Synthetic-only training does not pass this gate.
The gate must establish actual adaptation, not merely the presence of neural network classes.
The standard implementation should use the smallest effective models, targeting approximately 0.5-1B parameters or smaller.
Separately demonstrate that large adoption can arise through ordinary world mechanisms without forced view assignment.
Do not claim empirically realistic ten-million-view viral dynamics unless validated evidence supports that claim.
Demonstrate more than one product category.
Demonstrate a reference strategy achieving a feasible recurring-revenue objective in a generated world.
Do not treat that reference strategy as evidence that a learner learned to achieve it.
A renamed family or parameter variant does not count.
Reference trajectories must not be exposed as required solution paths.
Disconnected mini-environments behind a single dispatcher do not pass.
Numeric facility-only self-play does not pass.
This gate verifies integration, not the scientific success of any learning algorithm.
Before major benchmarks, establish machine-specific throughput targets based on measured hardware; do not weaken them after seeing results without change control.
The independent QA agent must run this gate after all implementation workstreams have been integrated.
Persistent engineering documents exist (MASTER_SPEC unchanged, ARCHITECTURE, INTERFACE_CONTRACTS, WORKSTREAMS, DECISION_LOG, PROGRESS, BLOCKERS, FIDELITY_REGISTER, ACCEPTANCE_MANIFEST, REPRODUCE).
Milestone state is persisted (branch, commit, workstreams, failures, remaining requirements, next actions, compute).
Three execution modes: controlled experimental environments, standalone semantic worlds, integrated civilizations.
Shared world substrate: common typed primitives, no duplicate shared facts, cross-module transactional integrity, recorded neural inference replayable without rerunning it.
Persistent individual identity with independently evolving state; individuals respond differently to the same situation and their preferences evolve through experience.
Four participant classes: vectorised behavioural, small adaptive neural, strategic neural, compact semantic.
Semantic-model choice benchmarked: task-specific encoders/policies, distilled tens-hundreds of millions, ~0.5-0.6B and ~1B models, on the eight listed capabilities.
Population profiles Development, Standard, Large and Internet scale with the specified sizes.

Independent learning tested separately: personal-state adaptation, shared-policy learning, independent policy groups, frozen historical participants, competing architectures; with weight hashes, losses and behaviour changes.

Interoperable platforms: short and long video, text posts, images, articles/blogs, forums, social networks, communities, messaging, search, creator subscriptions, newsletters, product discovery, developer communities, knowledge sharing.
Autonomous browsing behaviours (13 listed) with limited attention and time.
Artifacts of 10 kinds can be created, edited, rendered, published, updated, removed and inspected in the sandbox.

Recommendation mechanisms: chronological, interest retrieval, collaborative filtering, learned engagement, exploration, social graph, diversity-aware, reputation-sensitive, search-driven, freshness; delayed and noisy feedback.
Audience accounting distinguishes impressions, unique exposed, views, unique viewers, watch duration, completion, repeats, shares, subscribers, returning viewers; documented view threshold.
Communities with persistent membership, governance, moderation, trust, entry/exit, inactivity and participant-founded subjects.
Social-economic interoperability through ordinary mechanisms (no social-to-revenue bonus).
Fidelity record for every important behavioural mechanism, with evidence population, platform, period and limits.
Prespecified held-out metrics; learned models compared with simple baselines and the better one kept.

Businesses and products: formation, development, subscriptions, one-time purchases, licensing, marketplaces, SaaS, education/media/dev-tool/data/infrastructure/industrial products, contracts, refunds, cancellations, support, competition, bankruptcy.
General artifact-and-capability registry: a participant discovers a previously nonexistent service, tests it and adopts it if useful.
Emerging needs from reusable activity-resource-capability-constraint-need relations, not special-case triggers.
Software ecosystem: hosting, packages, dependency graphs, issues, PRs, review, tests, releases, docs, deployment, adoption by execution, maintenance, forks, compatibility, failures.
Adaptable institutions within stable constraints (cannot alter accounting, security, evaluation).
Versioned registry of the 28 composable causal primitives.
Eight new engine kinds: discrete-event, graph dynamical, search/information, executable program, multi-agent strategic, scientific experiment, planning/resource, partially observed state machine.
World admission checks (10 listed) with evaluator-side oracles only.
Tier 1 action interface covers graph edits, discrete, sequential, tool discovery, experiment design, queries, communication, programs, allocation, coordination.
Adjustable difficulty along nine axes; fast simulator and kernel agree where claimed.
Civilization profiles (10 listed) that differ structurally.
Multi-order chains include one with an agent-created artifact, one with social activity, one with technical or scientific activity, each confirmed by counterfactual removal.
Universal interaction contract (observe, execute, observe_since) across tiers carrying the 13 listed observation kinds with exact numbers.
Open-ended tool interface with discovery and schemas; agent-created services add discoverable affordances.
Reward modes legacy_shaped_reward, verified_terminal_outcome and observation_only.
Self-generated experiments: prediction, measurable outcome, deadline, execution, result retrieval, no reward for easy subgoals.
Long-horizon experience: durations, delayed events, asynchronous workflows, long-running programs, concurrent projects, commitments, provenance.
Documented path for future learners (including CAM) to connect without environment changes, proven by an external adapter that uses only the public interface.
Self-play population mixes current, historical, independent, statistical, compact neural, semantic and held-out policies.
No hidden coordination; controlled-identity transfers are not counted as independent success.
Resource scheduler enforcing CPU, RAM, GPU memory, GPU time, disk, inference concurrency and active worlds.
Performance report with the 12 listed quantities and a Crucible 4.0 comparison.
Versioned training-distribution registry across tiers with partitions and a sampler; evaluation reuse prevented.
Default tier mixture 50/30/20 with all tiers available.
World proposal interface validated for feasibility, diversity, safety, resources, difficulty and usefulness; cannot alter the evaluator or sealed distribution.
Learning-efficiency curves at 1-64 interactions and censoring-aware acceleration N_q ratios.
Executable A/B/C/D training-diversity comparison with matched experience and compute budgets and the seven listed controls.
Positive-control transfer experiment on newly added nontrivial families detected by the evaluator.
Security boundaries: default isolation from the public internet; real-world adapter disabled by default; consent, moderation and abuse prevention.
Final report contains the Part 18 completion table populated from verified evidence.
`python -m crucible.acceptance.v5 --verify-all` validates the manifest and evidence and exits nonzero whenever a requirement is not verified.

Observation-only mode is enabled by default across every environment family (Tier 1 rapid families, Tier 2 domains, Tier 3 civilization profiles, and the 4.0 environments exposed through crucible.experience).

No native or privileged reward signals reach the learner: no intermediate reward, shaping, action-quality score or goal-progress value through observations, auxiliary fields, tool responses or event metadata; Gymnasium scalar reward is 0.0.
Real observable consequences remain accessible: transactions, customer behaviour, technical measurements, social responses, resource changes, failures and delayed outcomes.
Independent outcome verification remains functional through a separate evaluator-side interface unreachable by the learner.
Agents can operate indefinitely within configured resource limits without an assigned objective.
An architecture-neutral external learner can supply its own training rewards and update its parameters with no environment change.
Delayed outcomes remain accessible for retrospective learning, linked to the originating actions by observable provenance.
Historical reward-based experiments remain reproducible through explicitly selected alternative modes (legacy_shaped_reward, verified_terminal_outcome).
Crucible is independent of CAM: no import of CAM code, and no acceptance gate depends on CAM's completion or success.
An independent audit classified every subsystem (RETAIN/REPAIR/EXTEND/REDESIGN/REBUILD/IMPLEMENT) on evidence before implementation resumed.
The progress ledger is maintained with the exact remaining requirements and next steps; milestones are committed and pushed to GitHub; no milestone work exists only in an uncommitted worktree.
Important fitted models, checkpoints and experimental artifacts are preserved in durable storage.
